en: The Praise of the Sādhana of Vajravilāsinī: From the pericarp of the firm filaments of the beautiful lady, radiant and blooming like the sun.
Marked by the rays of the newly full moon shimmering upon the peak of the mountain of sunrise. || 1 ||
Though familiar with the essences and liquors of various flowers,
the bee approached at the great festival of midnight, humming a sound that was swift, slow, and moderate.
"The mind is absorbed in that [object] while it is burning"—this is a marvel! || 2 ||
The moon rises and again goes to its setting; from that very place, it once more attains the crown of the mountain of sunrise,
when observed by the two ends of its crescent tail.
Neither does the moon shine, nor does the sun. || 3 ||
The sun rises within the interior of a lotus petal,
and the moon dissolves even from its peak;
and yonder submarine fire ascends upward.
Rāhu swallows the moon and the sun from below. || 4 ||

This first limb [of the practice] is the closing of the range of perception toward the manifest object of the eyes of the Lotus-seated One (Viṣṇu), who is the consort of Kamalinī; it is the union of the thunderbolt and the lotus.
Then follows the closing of the two eyes. || 5 ||
Instantly, through the friction of the seed-syllable of the practitioner, the triad attains the fourth state— the sky—
which is the innate series of digits of the imperishable abode.
Licking at the play of time that has been seized.
If the realization obtained from the mouth of a well-trained Vajravilāsinī guru has been attained,
then he who possesses that realization reaches the definitive certainty regarding the superior, middling, and inferior [levels], and thus becomes a seer of reality.
The Praise of the Sadhana of Śrī Vajravilāsinī is completed.
